cases.name: Maniriho Nkinamubanzi
cases.about:
Maniriho fled her home in the Democratic Republic of the
Congo as a refugee and had resettled along with her family
in Providence in 2015, where she worked as a laborer in
the food retail industry. According to the words of a friend
on her memorial page, Maniriho was “full of strength and
always smiling.”

"She was my best friend, my best friend," Joel Gemani said of Nkinamubanzi.

The two are both originally from Congo and Gemani said she considered Nkinamubanzi like a mother.

"I feel sad, very sad because she was my everything, because when I first came here I didn't have family here," said Gemani who worked with Nkinamubanzi at Tom’s Bao Bao in Providence.

In fact, the store manager said Nkinamubanzi, who had worked at the restaurant for the last five months, was like a mother figure to all her co-workers.

"Being a refugee, just being new to this country, she wanted to learn. She wanted to know and progress and do well for herself and for her children," said Shanice Fountain.
cases.narrative: On 11/17/2017, her body was found. Her oldest daughter called police to report her mother missing only to later discover her mother’s dead body concealed in a plastic bag under some laundry in a closet in her Providence, RI home.

cases.narrative: On 3/22/2022, Maddox's family told a Providence Police Department officer that Maddox had been killed and her body was inside Cooper's apartment on Parkis Avenue. Police made their way into his residence and located a .38 caliber revolver and a shotgun. They also reportedly noticed the fridge was no longer in the kitchen and instead in a Cooper's bedroom. The door was shut with a cord. Police opened the refrigerator and discovered Maddox's body "wrapped in several layers of plastic wrap and bedding."
